questions.q: What happens when you run CREATE SHARE with no further statements?
options: Nothing is exposed to any other account — the share starts empty until objects are explicitly granted to it
The entire database becomes visible to every Snowflake account
A full copy of the database is created for sharing
All existing roles automatically gain access to the share
questions.explain: A share is empty by design on creation — visibility requires explicit GRANT statements naming exactly what's exposed.

questions.q: What does a Snowflake share actually give a consumer account access to?
options: Live, direct query access to the provider's own storage — no data is copied
A nightly exported CSV file of the shared table
A read replica that syncs once a week
API-only access with no SQL querying
questions.explain: A share lets the consumer account query the provider's storage directly and live — there's no export or second copy involved.

questions.q: What statement adds a consumer account so it can actually use an already-populated share?
options: ALTER SHARE <name> ADD ACCOUNTS = '<account>'
GRANT CONSUME ON SHARE <name> TO ACCOUNT '<account>'
CREATE CONSUMER <account> FOR SHARE <name>
INSERT INTO <name> VALUES ('<account>')
questions.explain: ALTER SHARE ... ADD ACCOUNTS is the real, correct syntax for naming which consumer account(s) can access a populated share.

questions.q: What does the GRANTS_TO_SHARES ACCOUNT_USAGE view let you audit?
options: Every grant made to any share in the account, filterable to currently active grants with deleted_on IS NULL
Which warehouses are consuming the most compute credits
Only grants made in the last 24 hours, with no history
The row count of every shared table
questions.explain: GRANTS_TO_SHARES is structured like GRANTS_TO_USERS and GRANTS_TO_ROLES — it's the audit trail of what's been granted to shares, past and present.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does sharing through a secure view matter for a table with a masking policy?
options: The secure view's masking policy still evaluates for the consumer, so sensitive columns stay protected even when shared externally
Secure views make queries run faster for the consumer account
Masking policies only work when applied to shares, never to tables queried directly
A secure view removes the need to grant SELECT at all
questions.explain: Sharing a raw table bypasses whatever masking logic exists elsewhere; a secure view carries its masking policy with it, so the consumer still sees masked data.
